description: Regulation of Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-27 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka users already have access to Virtual Assets (VA), i.e. digital representation of value that can be digitally traded or transferred and can be used for payment and investment purposes, such as 'Cryptocurrencies’, through offshore exchanges and informal peer-to-peer online platforms. Since all such platforms are operating completely outside domestic regulatory perimeter, it is observed that Virtual Assets Service Providers are operating without registration requirements for Virtual Assets baseline compliance obligations, reporting standards, or supervisory oversight. Accordingly, in view of the risk of financial crimes likely to occur in the financial system of Sri Lanka, the need to establish a regulatory framework and a regulatory body for Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers has been identified. Therefore, under the policy guidance of the National Coordination Committee for Anti- Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism, a Sub-Committee on Virtual Asset Service Providers, chaired by the Deputy Minister of Digital Economy and other relevant officers, has been established to identify a regulatory framework and an implementation plan for Virtual Assets and Virtual Assets Service Providers. The Sub-Committee has proposed to designate the Securities and Exchange Commission of Sri Lanka as the Regulatory Authority for Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers, within a supervisory architecture coordinated by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka, the Financial Intelligence Unit and the Department of Inland Revenue. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Digital Economy, to take further action to introduce legal provisions to regulate Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers in Sri Lanka, taking into account the proposals submitted by the said Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.
